newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Belgrade forms body to cooperate on war crimes.
newsitem.headline: Belgrade forms body to cooperate on war crimes.

text.p: The government of Yugoslavia, comprising Serbia and Montenegro, has formed a commission to improve cooperation with an international war crimes tribunal, state media reported on Thursday.
"The Yugoslav government has decided to establish a commission for cooperation for the International War Crimes Tribunal in former Yugoslavia (ICTY)," state news agency Tanjug said.
The commission was set up "with the aim of implementing the Dayton agreement and the agreement with the United Nations on opening a war crimes tribunal office in Belgrade," the agency said.
Yugoslavia has long refused to cooperate with the tribunal set up two years ago in The Hague, the first such court since World War Two.
Belgrade is obliged to cooperate fully with the tribunal under the Dayton peace accord hammered out in Ohio in November 1995
The court has indicted more than 70 people for war crimes in Bosnia and Croatia. Three of them are senior officers of the former Yugoslav national army believed to be at large in Serbia.
Belgrade has so far refused to hand them over claiming the country's constitution prohibits extradition of its nationals to other countries.

"The commission will monitor the realization of accords, coordinate the activities of federal and other competent organs on their implementation, review questions of importance to cooperation with the ICTY," Tanjug quoted a government statement as saying.

Belgrade is under severe pressure from the West to improve its human rights record after 53 days of mass protests in Serbia over the annulment of opposition victories in local elections last November.
